chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Siqall from his father from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man who divorces his wife while she is pregnant, he said: He divorces her. I asked: And if he revokes the divorce? He said: Yes, he revokes the divorce. I asked: If it occurs to him after he has revoked it to divorce her again, he said: No, until she gives birth.

It was said to him: The meaning in this report is that he does not have the right to divorce her with any type of divorce. And if that is not the case, we interpret it as meaning he does not have the right to divorce her with the divorce of the Sunnah if he has already revoked it until she gives birth. As for the divorce of the waiting period, it is permissible if he has had intercourse with her, and this indicates that.

key_terms.طَلَاقُ الْعِدَّةِ: Divorce of the waiting period (irrevocable divorce)
key_terms.يُرَاجِعُهَا: He revokes the divorce (takes her back)

ai.seo_question: Can a man divorce his pregnant wife multiple times before she gives birth?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *al-Istibsar*, clarifying the juristic deduction that a man cannot issue a revocable divorce to his pregnant wife after the initial revocation until she gives birth, based on the principle that the waiting period extends until delivery. The text further distinguishes this from an irrevocable divorce, which is permissible if he has consummated the marriage, highlighting the nuanced application of *iddah* (waiting period) rules for pregnant women in Shia jurisprudence. This discussion underscores the importance of distinguishing between *talaq al-sunna* and *talaq al-'iddah* to ensure the validity of the divorce and the determination of paternity.
